text:
Washington won this one by three goals in 10 minutes of the second period, which is about the only stretch where the numbers favored them. Everywhere else, New Jersey played the better game. The Devils out-attempted the Capitals 80 to 42, led in expected goals 4.13 to 2.29, and deserved to win in 78 percent of simulated replays. WSH took the real one anyway.

The goals came fast. After Arseny Gritsyuk opened the scoring on a 1 percent snap shot, Ryan Leonard tied it on the power play late in the first. Ilya Protas made it 2-1 early in the second, Dylan Strome added a backhand a little over three minutes later, and Boone Jenner's snap shot at 11:14 made it 4-1. That period was the one stretch Washington won on chance quality, 1.09 to 0.71, and the goals arrived at a better rate than the chances alone would suggest. Vincent Desharnais picked up assists on two of them.

New Jersey pushed hard from there. The Devils posted 2.31 expected goals in the third to Washington's 0.55, and Dawson Mercer missed the net on a 32 percent look. Logan Thompson stopped 29 of 31 shots, 2.13 goals better than expected, and was named first star. Timo Meier's power-play goal with 19 seconds left only made the score look closer.
